look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: SEASONAL SEQUENCE. (1) Autumn/winter flat rosette of elongated, often unevenly TOOTHED lower leaves; (2) one erect leafy stem with many NARROW, ALTERNATE, sessile stem leaves, smaller toward tip; (3) large upper panicle of numerous TINY greenish capitula, with an involucre ~3–4 mm LONG and rays usually too short to see without a hand lens; (4) white fluffy pappus as fruits mature. Compare a rooted plant and actual flowering heads before confirming an ambiguous rosette. No bright yellow goldenrod plume.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Annual or winter annual, commonly from a small taproot, overwintering flat rosette before bolting; not a long-lived basal clump.

key_traits.label: Basal
key_traits.text: Early leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, often shallow teeth, up to ~10 cm; basal leaves often shrivel as plant flowers.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: One generally straight, unbranched lower stem, leafy with many narrow alternate sessile leaves. Branches concentrated near the TOP in a loose tapering panicle (not grass spike or yellow goldenrod raceme).

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, linear to narrowly oblanceolate, lower 20–50(-100) × 4–10(-15) mm, upper progressively narrower, edges sometimes toothed or ciliate with stiff marginal hairs; surfaces often almost smooth except veins.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Many tiny heads in a terminal panicle; the INVOLUCRE (the bract cup beneath one head) is about 3–4 mm LONG, not necessarily a 3–4 mm diameter for the full head. Marginal very short white or pinkish ray-floret tips ~0.5–1 mm usually hard to see without magnification; central tubular florets present. Distinguish fresh flowers from ripe silky pappus.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Dry one-seeded cypsela ~1–1.5 mm with one ring of fine white pappus bristles usually ~2–3 mm; wind distributed.

key_traits.label: Site
key_traits.text: Disturbed open ground, roadsides, empty beds, old fields, turf gaps, margins. Disturbance-tolerant early successional plant, but not by itself a determination of native-zone certification.

key_traits.label: Variation
key_traits.text: Flower heads and stems vary with age, drought and site; non-native-looking labels on overseas photographs describe local status abroad, not species' North American origin.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Early basal TOOTHED rosette; narrow ALTERNATE stem leaves and single central stem; pyramid of MANY very small whitish heads (not a yellow display); minute inconspicuous rays; white fuzzy pappus after seed maturation

lookalikes.differences: On a mature plant, horseweed usually has ONE tall leafy axis, many narrow ALTERNATE leaves, and scores of tiny terminal heads (involucre ~3–4 mm long) with barely projecting whitish ray florets. E. strigosus, E. philadelphicus and E. annuus typically present fewer, larger, clearly daisy-like heads with visible projecting rays; a rosette alone is not a confident separation. E. geiseri is annual but has visibly longer fleabane rays; E. modestus has a woody perennial root crown. Goldenrods (Solidago) have conspicuous yellow rays in yellow flowering sprays. Similar small-headed Conyza/Erigeron bonariensis/sumatrensis should be keyed with hair and phyllary detail; their occurrence here is not asserted.
